title: NY State Assembly · District 79
area: The Bronx: Concourse Village, Melrose, Morrisania, Claremont, Belmont, and East Tremont

context.text: Both parties' primaries scheduled for June 23, 2026 were canceled. Incumbent Chantel Jackson (D) advanced without appearing on the ballot. Emmanuel Findlay Jr. withdrew from the Republican primary but advanced from the Conservative Party primary without appearing on the ballot, so he appears on the Conservative Party line only.

candidates.name: Chantel Jackson
candidates.currentRole: Member, NY State Assembly, District 79 (since January 2021)

summary.text: Chantel Jackson is the incumbent Democratic Assembly Member for District 79 in the Bronx, seeking a fourth term. A licensed social worker and former college advisor, she first won the seat in 2020. She chairs the New York State Legislative Women's Caucus and previously chaired the Black Legislative Task Force, and her official biography lists maternal health, economic development, mental health and youth development as her focus areas.

background.text: Born in Harlem and raised in a close-knit family; her mother immigrated from Belize and her late father, who died in 2022, was an entrepreneur and CEO of WIBO. In her 2020 Ballotpedia survey she described herself as living in the South Bronx.
Earned a bachelor's degree in psychology from the City College of New York and a Master of Social Work from Adelphi University (Ballotpedia lists 2014).
Spent nine years working with low-income, first-generation students on college access and financial aid before becoming a social worker.

Worked as a licensed social worker in New York City public high schools for four years, and has also taught at the college level and written a book, according to her official biography and 2020 survey.

Won the June 2020 Democratic primary for the open Assembly District 79 seat with 25.9% of the vote in a six-candidate field, and the November 2020 general election with 89.8%; Ballotpedia lists her term as beginning January 1, 2021.
Re-elected in 2022 (87.1% over Republican Richard Bryan) and in 2024 (80.1% over Republican Sharon Darby and Conservative Party candidate Emmanuel Findlay Jr.).
Sits on the Assembly's Cities, Education, Housing, Mental Health, and Small Business committees, and chairs the Subcommittee on Micro Business.

Chaired the New York State Black Legislative Task Force during what her official biography calls the past legislative session, and the biography says she helped secure a $30 million investment for underserved communities, and has chaired the Legislative Women's Caucus since June 2025. She championed A7713, on adolescent offender case processing.

Her official biography says she organized two buses of Bronx students to Invest Fest in Atlanta in August 2024 and hosted The Next Wave Career Summit in February 2026; it describes her as a licensed social worker, college professor, published author and mother of two.

priorities.text: Now in her third term at the time of the profile, Jackson focuses on maternal health, economic development, mental health, youth development, and holistic wellness.

As Chair of the New York State Black Legislative Task Force, she helped secure a $30 million investment for underserved communities and led a 12-stop statewide listening tour to ensure the funding reflected local needs.

In February 2026 she hosted The Next Wave Career Summit, bringing together professionals in content creation, photography, and entrepreneurship to equip students with tools and pathways into those fields.

Co-writing with state Sen. Cordell Cleare, Jackson said Albany budget proposals "restored funding to Aid and Incentives to Municipalities, increased tax revenue to New York City, restored funding for foster care, adult shelter costs, cash assistance for low-income families, and more — driving more than $5 billion more toward our city," arguing the state had shortchanged New York City and that Black families face the city's steepest affordability pressures.

positions.summary: In a 2020 candidate survey, said New York had passed progressive tenant protection laws and pledged to work to see them enforced in the Bronx.
positions.quote: New York State has passed some of the most progressive tenant protection laws, and Chantel will work to ensure they are being upheld in the Bronx.

positions.summary: In a 2020 candidate survey, said she wants to properly fund mental health services and increase insurance coverage for uninsured and underinsured people.
positions.quote: She wants to properly fund mental health services and increase insurance for uninsured and underinsured people.

record.text: Sponsored A7713, which changed adolescent-offender plea and Family Court removal procedures; it passed the Assembly and Senate and was signed into law (Chapter 809 of 2021).

Is the Assembly sponsor of A2140 (Fair Pricing Act, same as S705), which would cap prices for a set of routine outpatient medical services at 150% of the Medicare rate; the bill was reported to the Codes Committee on May 27, 2026.
As of the 2025-2026 session, serves on the Assembly's Cities, Education, Housing, Mental Health, and Small Business committees, and chairs the Subcommittee on Micro Business.

candidates.name: Emmanuel Findlay Jr.

summary.text: Emmanuel Findlay Jr. is the Conservative Party candidate for Assembly District 79. Ballotpedia lists him as a candidate for New York City Council District 16 in 2025 on the Republican and Conservative lines and for this Assembly seat in 2024 on the Conservative line; he lost both races.

background.text: In the November 2025 general election for New York City Council District 16, Findlay received 11.4% of the vote (2,357 votes) running on the Republican and Conservative Party lines, losing to incumbent Althea Stevens.
In the November 2024 general election for this Assembly seat, Findlay received 3.3% of the vote (841 votes) on the Conservative Party line, behind Chantel Jackson (D) and Sharon Darby (R).
Appears on the November 3, 2026 ballot on the Conservative Party line only; he withdrew from the Republican primary and advanced from the Conservative Party primary without appearing on the ballot.

candidates.researchNotes: No Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response, campaign website, or news coverage of policy positions could be located for Findlay as of September 25, 2026; his Ballotpedia page lists only personal Facebook and Instagram accounts, with no linked campaign site.

researchNotes: Jackson has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; her only completed survey, from 2020, is dated but the tenant-protection and health-coverage statements it contains are consistent with her later record and are cited above. No other source found gives a direct, on-the-record stance matching this guide's other fixed issue keys, so no further Position entries are included; her priorities and record are otherwise documented in depth. Findlay has no campaign website, has not completed Ballotpedia's survey in any cycle, and has no record of prior officeholding, so his entry is marked 'minimal.' No biographical details for Findlay (birthplace, education, occupation) were found in any loaded source.
